title: Cold rebuild: pool sizing
summary: Rebuild the connection-pool calculator from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove it stuck. You built **the pool-sizing functions** in *Connections and pools*. Now write them
again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones
Why: the next time an autoscaler doubles your app tier, you need this arithmetic in your head before the
database starts refusing connections. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Each app instance runs 600 queries per second averaging 8 ms. With 50 % headroom, what pool size per instance does Little's law suggest?
steps.explain: 600 × 0.008 s = 4.8 busy connections on average; × 1.5 = 7.2, rounded up to 8.

steps.prompt: Database CPU is at 100 % and queries are slow. Someone proposes raising every app's pool from 10 to 40. What happens?
options: Queries get slower: more concurrent work on saturated CPUs adds contention, and the extra connections cost memory
steps.explain: Pools help when connections are the bottleneck. When the database itself is the bottleneck, let requests wait in the app's pool and fix the work (indexes, caching, replicas).

steps.title: Cold rebuild: size the pools
